chunks: From him, from Mu'awiya ibn Hakim, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from Yahya al-Azraq, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about a man who was killed while he had a debt upon him, and his heirs took the blood money (diyah); is his debt paid? He said, 'Yes, they only took his blood money.'

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاؤُهُ: Heirs or legal guardians of the deceased
key_terms.الدِّيَةَ: Blood money or compensation paid for killing
key_terms.دَيْنٌ: Debt or liability owed by the deceased

ai.seo_question: Does blood money (diyah) go to pay off the debts of the deceased before heirs receive it?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that blood money (diyah) is treated as the deceased's personal property, thereby subject to the same priority of debt repayment as other assets. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that the creditor's right to repayment takes precedence over the heirs' entitlement to the estate, ensuring financial obligations are settled before inheritance distribution. The narration highlights the continuity of the deceased's legal personality regarding their liabilities, even after death.
